subject: Re: Bulk inference completion SLA — escrow + safe-retry proposal
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@clearsky.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearsky.com
Date: Wed, 08 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Bulk inference SLA for monthly batch jobs

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Clearsky is close to selecting a vendor for our monthly anonymized inference runs. Before we proceed we'd like a clear commitment that a submitted nightly bulk job (<= 10M tokens) will either: complete within 6 hours OR incur a service credit.

Specific asks:
- Defined completion window (6h target, 12h hard limit)
- Retry semantics and at-least-once vs at-most-once behavior
- Guidance on idempotency tokens and safe-retry recommendations for our ingestion pipeline
- Escalation path if jobs exceed the hard limit (points of contact + remediation timeline)

I've attached our requirements doc (SLA_requirements.pdf). Can Redwood support a temporary carveout for batch completion SLAs for the first 6 months while we finalize integration? If so, what remediation/credits procedure would you propose?

We need a draft amendment to share with procurement by Feb 15.

Best,
Alice Zhang
Head of Data Infrastructure
Clearsky Analytics

Attachment: SLA_requirements.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@clearsky.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Bulk inference SLA for monthly batch jobs

Alice — thanks for the clear asks and the doc. Short answer: we can propose a limited, operationally-safe amendment that provides a defined completion window and a measurable remediation path, but it will include a conditional approach while your integration stabilizes.

High-level proposal (for discussion):
1) Escrowed completion SLA: target completion = 6 hours; contractual credit applies after 12 hours. For the first 6 months we offer this on a best-effort basis with defined test milestones.
2) Safe-retry + idempotency: require a per-job idempotency token (X-Redwood-Idempotency) and conversation-id in metadata. We'll publish a recommended client-side backoff (exponential, capped at 6 retries) and server-side dedupe window (24 hours) that we will honor.
3) Remediation workflow: automated credits calculated per-job when hard limit exceeded + a post-mortem within 48 hours for systemic failures.
4) Test-run gating: a shadow test run of your typical batch within a staging window (we'll provide tooling and a test-run checklist).

I've attached a rough ops sketch (proposed-escrow-ops.md) that outlines how the escrow SLA would be enforced, and a suggested amendment template. Could you share the top 3 failure modes you worry about so we can tune thresholds? We'll loop Legal/Procurement next and produce a DocuSign-ready amendment by Feb 14.

- Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-escrow-ops.md (Markdown, 6KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Bulk inference SLA for monthly batch jobs

Vivek / Dev — looping Rishi since this touches runtime guarantees and chargeback. A few operational notes from infra:

- We can realistically surface a 6h median completion target for their workload shape, but the hard 12h cap must include exceptions for force-majeure and multi-tenant capacity spikes. Contract should explicitly allow for protected maintenance windows.
- For idempotency: our recommended header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) + job-level checksum is fine. We should document precisely how we dedupe (retain KV of recent job ids for 48h, TTL-based).
- Credits: propose a per-job credit formula tied to tokens processed (e.g., 0.5% of the job invoice per hour beyond 12h, capped at 25% per incident). That aligns incentives without opening unlimited exposure.
- Retry semantics: server will accept repeated submissions with the same idempotency token and will not re-run if previous run completed. If a retry is submitted while the previous run is still processing, we will de-dupe at ingest and return a 202 with existing job id.

Operational asks for procurement:
1) Agreed-upon test data set and a baseline SLA run in staging (we should both run 3 consecutive nightly jobs within SLA before production enforcement).
2) Access to a read-only telemetry feed for the job (latency distribution, queue depth) for the first 90 days.

If procurement insists on hard financial SLOs immediately, we should offer an interim 'SLA escrow' — credits held in escrow and released after joint verification of breach. That gives procurement comfort while we complete integration.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Feb 2028 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Draft amendment + safe-retry operational checklist

Alice / Clearsky procurement — attached is a draft amendment that implements the escrowed completion SLA along with an operationally-safe retry policy. Highlights:

- Contract language: target = 6 hours; remediation credit triggers after 12 hours (formula included). Exclusions are listed (maintenance, force majeure, customer-side malformed payloads).
- Escrow mechanics: Redwood will set aside a remediation pool equivalent to 2x expected monthly batch spend for the first 90 days. Credits are applied per-job after joint verification.
- Idempotency and retries: client must supply X-Redwood-Idempotency and content-hash. Recommended client-side backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s (max 6 retries). Server dedupe window = 24 hours.
- Observability: we will provide a read-only telemetry stream and a test-run checklist (test-run-checklist.csv) to validate production-equivalent latency distribution.

Next steps:
1) Can Procurement confirm they accept the escrow construct and the credit formula?
2) Agree test dates for two staging runs (we propose Feb 21-22).
3) Legal to review the amendment; we will push a DocuSign link once legal gives the green light.

DocuSign draft: https://app.docusign.com/clearsky/amendment/CLSK-47

Thanks — I scheduled the staging window tentatively and attached the amendment draft and checklist.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 18KB); test-run-checklist.csv (CSV, 2KB)

Vivek — thanks, this looks reasonable and addresses most of our concerns. Procurement is OK with the escrow concept in principle; Legal wants to review the exact exclusion language. Two quick asks before we sign:

1) Can we run a single production-equivalent night on Feb 22 (not just staging) under a joint run-play to see end-to-end behavior? We can mark it as a non-production-impacting run (read-only) if needed, but we'd like to see queue depth/latency across our payloads.
2) Please surface the telemetry feed endpoint and auth details ahead of the run (so our SREs can wire dashboards).

If the run looks good, Procurement is ready to accept the amendment pending Legal review. Please send the DocuSign link when ready.

Thanks,
